title: Streaming token audit horizon correction and multi-source attribution
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent mismatches between billed token counts and downstream ledger reconciliations for long-lived streaming sessions that ingest tokens from multiple sources (client original input, proxy prompt rewrites, and server-side retrievals). Root cause hypothesis: the current rounding and anchoring logic uses a per-frame crediting horizon that fails when late fragments arrive after a rate-limiter stall or when retokenization occurs in the proxy path. Consequences: orphaned provisional credits, incorrect quota consumption, and customer support tickets for phantom charges.

Goals:
- Define a canonical "audit horizon" that anchors token attribution for a stream session across sources and across reconnects.
- Ensure deterministic finalization semantics for late fragments, retokenized inputs, and mid-stream model variant switches.
- Add guardrails so the rate limiter and quota engine don't permanently over- or under-charge during stall/retry cycles.

Scope and non-goals:
In-scope: streaming WebSocket/frame ingestion, proxy-rewrites that alter token counts, server-side retrievals appended mid-stream, and the ledger finalization step. Out-of-scope: batch synchronous inference endpoints and embedding-only pipelines (handled by separate work).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Introduce a session-level Audit Horizon window (default 60s) tracked in the session state machine. The horizon anchors the token provenance pointer: any late fragment that arrives within the horizon is applied to the original session attribution; fragments after the horizon create an "after-horizon" reconciliation flow that requires a finalization pass and a provisional rollback if needed.
2) Canonicalize token counting to a single tokenization pass in the ingress layer. If a proxy or transformation re-tokenizes (e.g., prompt rewriting or compression), both the original and transformed token counts are recorded with a provenance tag; final ledger attribution uses the canonicalized ingress tokenization unless an authorized transformer (trusted proxy) explicitly marks a delta reconciliation event.
3) Introduce a rate-limiter-aware checkpoint: when rate limiter stalls or backpressure occurs, we snapshot outstanding provisional credits and mark them with the current clock and horizon. If the client reconnects and resumes within horizon, credits are reconciled to the resumed stream id; otherwise they enter the after-horizon reconciliation path.
4) Add deterministic finalizer that resolves provisional credits using: (a) canonical token counts, (b) fragment ordering by server-provided monotonic offset, and (c) signed provenance markers for transformer components.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- 60s horizon default balances latency and practical recovery windows for mobile/ flaky networks; shorter horizon risks false orphaning, longer horizon increases complexity and memory on session store. We will make horizon configurable per-tenant.
- Single ingress tokenization simplifies downstream accounting but requires the ingress layer to support tokenizer variants and fallback paths for multi-tokenizer clients. This avoids double-counting from retokenization.
- Reconciliation step increases complexity of ledger finalizer but keeps runtime fast-path common-case unchanged; reconciliation runs in background and emits audit events for visibility.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for Done):
- Deterministic reconciliation reproduces token tallies for a set of 10 fuzz scenarios (attached) including: reconnect-within-horizon, reconnect-after-horizon, proxy-retokenize-no-delta, proxy-retokenize-with-delta, midstream-model-switch, server-append-retrieval-after-stall. (List provided in acceptance_criteria.)
- End-to-end integration test that simulates a rate-limiter stall and confirms no phantom final charges after a resumed stream (allowed variance < 0.1% over 1k simulated sessions).
- Dashboard panel added to Console showing "Audit Horizon events" with drilldowns to session id, provisional credits, and reconciliation outcome.
- Documentation (internal Confluence) and runbook updated for support teams describing how to interpret audit events and trigger manual reconciliations.

Implementation notes (detailed):
- session_state.proto: add fields audit_horizon_ts, provisional_credit_snapshot (opaque token counts + offsets + provenance hash).
- ingress/tokenizer service: add canonicalize flag; emit tokenization_provenance header on requests passing to runtime.
- ledger/finalizer: add reconciliation queue + idempotent reconciliation handler that consumes after-horizon events and produces minimal corrective transactions (refunds or top-ups).
- rate_limiter: when stall triggers (>N ms queueing), persist provisional snapshot to durable session store with horizon expiry.
- telemetry: emit metering.audit.horizon.{created,resolved,expired} and include session latency and originating transformer id.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for canonical tokenization and provenance header propagation.
- Deterministic integration harness that replays captured stream traces and checks ledger after finalization.
- Production canary on small dedicated capacity customers and internal dev orgs for 48h with high telemetry sampling.

Notes on rollback and customer remediation:
If reconciliation produces a customer-visible correction, attach automated support ticket linking session ids, delta amounts, and the audit timeline. Refunds should be batched into daily settlement transactions rather than immediate micro-refunds to reduce ops load.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzz harness reproduces token tallies for 10 synthetic scenarios with <0.1% variance over 1k runs
Rate-limiter stall + resume within horizon results in no net extra charge (test harness)
Ingress emits tokenization_provenance header for all transformed streams
Console shows Audit Horizon events with ability to query by session id and reconciliation status
Reconciliation handler is idempotent when replayed against same after-horizon event
implementation_notes: Add audit_horizon_ts and provisional_credit_snapshot to session_state.proto
Ingress exposes canonicalize tokenizer mode and emits tokenization_provenance header
Ledger finalizer picks up reconciliation queue and writes corrective transactions with provenance references
Rate limiter will persist a provisional snapshot on stall with configurable horizon TTL
Emit telemetry metering.audit.horizon.created/resolved/expired with session and tenant tags
